we give a work-optimal algorithm for the selection problem in sorted matrices, which improves upon the result of (Sarnath & He, 1993) for the case m ⩾ n and generalizes their result for the case m = n.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the case of selection on sorted matrices, the dimension of the matrices is not a limiting factor in designing work-optimal parallel algorithms.

the parallel selection algorithm can be made optimal in terms of the number of operations and the number of processors, and can be made to run in time that is optimal in terms of log n and poly log n.
the problem of selection on sorted matrices is not just a special case of the problem of selection from an arbitrary array, but is a fundamental problem in its own right.
